nodes.description: Manganese shifts alpha-synuclein towards its aggregation-prone conformation. This is the point where manganism and the synucleinopathies come closest, and it is worth being careful: aggregation is documented in the cortex of exposed primates, while the human neuropathology of manganism is specifically Lewy-body negative. The two are compatible only if the aggregates here are not Lewy bodies.

nodes.description: Loss of the two transporters that clear synaptic glutamate, GLAST (SLC1A3) and GLT-1 (SLC1A2). Glutamate then accumulates outside the cell not because more is released but because less is removed.

Astrocytes are the metal's reservoir, concentrating it far above neuronal levels because they carry the transporters. That is protective up to a point and then becomes the mechanism: a loaded astrocyte stops doing its day job, which in the basal ganglia is clearing glutamate.

nodes.description: The final common pathway for the motor syndrome. Because the damage is at and beyond the pallidum rather than upstream of the dopamine synapse, supplying more dopamine precursor does not restore the circuit - which is the mechanistic reason levodopa disappoints here.

nodes.description: The standard chelator, and a treatment whose evidence base sits mostly in the inherited disease rather than the occupational one. It lowers blood manganese; it does not cross the blood-brain barrier well, which is the usual explanation for why the biochemical response outruns the clinical one in established manganism.

nodes.description: Sustained intake above what homeostasis clears. Occupationally this is inhaled welding fume or ore dust; the particles are small enough that most of an inhaled dose is retained in the lung, from which manganese reaches the blood without passing the gut and liver first. The exposure is measured in months to years, not in single doses.

evidence.reference_title: Manganese Neurotoxicity: A Comprehensive Review of Pathophysiology and Inherited and Acquired Disorders.

nodes.description: Reported as part of the prodrome rather than as a late consequence, which is what makes it mechanistically interesting: the cognitive and psychiatric disturbance characteristically arrives before the movement disorder that gets the disease its name.

Primate work puts manganese-induced alpha-synuclein aggregates in frontal cortex grey and white matter, which is a plausible substrate, though the link to the human psychiatric picture is not established.

The florid end of the prodrome, and the source of the disease's older names. It sits beside `Hallucinations` rather than replacing it: the cited sentence names delusions, while the hallucination claim still rests on a source that says "psychiatric symptoms" without naming them.

The evidence here is weaker than for the other motor features and the entry says so: the occupational cohorts record "impairment of speech" without separating articulation from volume, and the one source that names dysarthria outright is describing the inherited childhood form.

nodes.description: Structural damage to the pallidum, with the internal segment preferentially affected, and with the substantia nigra pars compacta spared and no Lewy bodies. This is the neuropathological core of the disease and the fact that separates it from Parkinson disease.

nodes.description: Sustained overstimulation of postsynaptic glutamate receptors, with the calcium load and cell death that follow. This is the non-cell-autonomous half of the lesion: the neuron dies from a failure in the astrocyte beside it.

Part of the neuropsychiatric prodrome that historically preceded the motor syndrome and gave manganism its older names. MONDO's own definition lists confusion and hallucinations before the extrapyramidal features.

nodes.description: The other way to reach overload: normal intake with a broken exit. Manganese is cleared in bile, so chronic liver failure raises body burden without any unusual exposure, and parenteral nutrition delivers manganese straight into the blood past the gut and liver entirely. Both produce the same pallidal accumulation as the occupational route.

nodes.description: Dopaminergic terminals that are present but underperforming. This is the finding that stops manganism being a simple postsynaptic story: imaging in exposed people and primates shows the terminals are there, while dopamine release is markedly reduced. A functional presynaptic deficit, not a degenerative one.

nodes.description: A drug-preparation route rather than an industrial one, and the highest-dose human exposure on record. Home synthesis of methcathinone oxidises ephedrine with potassium permanganate and the manganese goes into the product, which is then injected. It produces the same syndrome faster and more severely, and it is the setting in which the imaging and levodopa-response evidence is clearest.

nodes.description: Adjunctive, and mechanistically the neatest intervention in the entry: manganese rides the iron transporters, so raising iron status competes it off them. That is the same DMT1 iron-dependence this entry's transport node records, read backwards as a therapy. The evidence is a review's treatment recommendation rather than a trial, and the clearest demonstrations are in the inherited transporter defects.

nodes.description: Included because its failure is diagnostically informative rather than because it works. A patient whose parkinsonism is manganese-related characteristically does not respond, and that non-response has been used as a discriminating criterion against Parkinson disease. The mechanism predicts it: the lesion is at and beyond the pallidum, so replenishing the dopamine precursor does not reach the problem.

nodes.description: Manganese travels on carriers it does not own. Several transporters move it and few are selective for it - DMT1, ZIP8, ZIP14, transferrin receptor, all built for iron or zinc - which is why iron status changes the dose that reaches the brain and why the metal lands where those carriers are densest rather than where it would do least harm.

nodes.description: Divalent manganese drives hydrogen peroxide production in the mitochondrial fraction of microglia, and the route is specifically complex II: the effect is supported by the complex II substrate succinate and abolished by complex II inhibition, while complex I substrates do not support it and complex I inhibition does not abolish it. The resulting microglial free-radical output in turn facilitates dopaminergic neurotoxicity. This is a narrower claim than the general oxidative-stress node, about a named respiratory complex in a named cell type, which is why the two are kept apart.

nodes.description: Manganese impairs mitochondrial respiration and generates reactive oxygen species. The basal ganglia are a bad place for this to happen: high oxygen consumption, and in the dopaminergic compartment a transmitter that oxidises into radicals of its own.

nodes.description: Activated astrocytes and microglia releasing cytokines and nitric oxide synthase products into the pallidum. It is a consequence of the metal load and then an independent source of injury.

The classical route and the one MONDO's definition is written around: welding, mining, ore processing, battery manufacture, ferromanganese smelting. What makes inhalation special is not the dose but the anatomy - it delivers manganese to the blood without the gut absorption control and hepatobiliary first-pass that handle dietary intake.

nodes.description: The defining lesion location. Manganese concentrates in the basal ganglia and most of all in the globus pallidus, where it sits in GABAergic neurons and in astrocytes. Because manganese is paramagnetic, the accumulation is directly visible as symmetric T1 hyperintensity on MRI, which is what makes the imaging finding a measure of the metal rather than of its consequences.

nodes.description: The only intervention with an unambiguous rationale, and the reason occupational hygiene rather than neurology is where this disease is won. It does not reliably reverse established damage - the two cached series that followed patients after cessation report non-resolution and, in one, progression through the first decade - but it stops the burden rising, and it is the one step available before symptoms appear.

nodes.description: Present, but not the tremor of Parkinson disease. Where manganism tremor is described it is a rapid postural tremor; resting tremor is specifically reported as not characteristic, and that asymmetry is one of the discriminators the differential leans on. One review states flatly that patients with manganism have no tremor at all, which is recorded here as a REFUTE rather than reconciled - see the `tremor_in_manganism` discussion.
